name: derivation_thresholds
description: Version 5 (Story 5.1): version 4's thirteen parameters unchanged, plus the one the dashboard's fraud-flag derivation reads. Superseding is a new document, never an edit — v1 through v4 stay exactly what Stories 2.1, 2.2, 2.5 and 3.1 shipped, so an ordering, a banner, a forms card or a benefit figure produced under any of them is still explainable. fraudFlagScoreMin is the fraud score at or above which a fraud-flagged claim counts as FLAGGED FOR REVIEW on the portfolio dashboard. It is deliberately NOT siuFraudScoreMin, and the two must not be collapsed: siuFraudScoreMin (60) is the SIU *referral* threshold that earns a queue card its +35 priority weight and its SIU chip, while this one (55) is the wider review population the supervisor's Fraud Flags card counts — 13 seeded claims against the referral rule's 9. Two rules over one column pair, each with its own threshold, exactly as the prototype has them (queue chip: fraudFlag && fraudScore>=60, line 953; dashboard card caption: 'Score >= 55 - review needed', line 1069). It lives in THIS document rather than in one of its own because fraud_flagged is a registered derivation (AD-10) and DerivationThresholds is the single argument every registered derivation is built from — the same argument v3 made for the path parameters and v4 for the PTD cut-off. Putting the number here is what stops the dashboard aggregate from comparing a score itself, which would leave half a rule in services/worklist where nothing checks it.
